To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phosphorylation of cardiac sarcoplamic reticulum by cAMP-dependent kinase results in a stimulation of the initial rate and levels of acid-stable phosphorylation of the Ca2+ ATPase, and that this stimulation results from an increase in the apparent affinity of the Ca2+/Mg2+ binding sites of the Ca2 + ATPase and an increase in the rate constant for the formation of the E-P intermediate of the Ca2 +-ATPase.

phosphorylation of SR Ca2+-ATPhase by cAMP-dependent kinase increases the affinity of SR Ca2+ pump for Ca2+, increases the number of Ca2+ binding sites, increases the initial rate of formation and decomposition of the phosphorylated enzyme (EP), and results in an overall stimulation at steady state.

phosphorylation of canine cardiac SR by cAM-dependent protein kinase increases the initial rate of formation of the acid-stuble phosphorylated enzyme (EP), decreases the dissociation constant of Ca2+ for EP formation, increases the initial rate and steady state level of EP decomposition, and decreases the dissociation of the Ca2+ complex from EP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which adenosine 2',5'-monphosphate (cAMP)-dependent protein kinase stimulates the initial rate of calcium uptake and Ca2+ -ATPase activity in canine cardiac sarcoplasm.
the mechanism of the cAMP-mediated stimulation of the calcium ion dependent adenylyl transferase of cardiac sarcoplasmaic reticulum.

elucidating the mechanism of regulation of Ca2+-dependent adenosine 1,3,5'-triphosphatase (Ca2+-ATP) of cardiac sarcoplamic reticulum (CaSR) by adenosine-3',5'- monophosphate (AMP)-dependent protein kinase (PK).

phosphorylation of the Ca2+ ATPase in cardiac sarcoplasm increases the affinity of the Ca2+/Mg2+ binding site, thereby increasing the rate of phosphorylation of the enzyme and increasing the rate of Ca2+-uptake.
